paragraphs: Ben Elasa, wise, wealthy, our holy master’s son-in-law. They said he did not spend his money in vain learning the high priest’s haircut: one hair’s tip beside another’s root, Nedarim 51a. Rashi implies he paid his barber much for that cut. Shabbat 9b; Shocher Tov, section 9, he was asked by a philosopher [the checked Midrash calls the questioner Philippos]. See Jerusalem Talmud, beginning of Megallechin: bar Kappara mocked him; Rabbi rebuked bar Kappara, who understood he would not be ordained in Rabbi’s days.
